question: In the United States, for Q4 2019 and Q4 2020, first select only those cities where total sales (with no promotions) rose by at least 20% from Q4 2019 to Q4 2020. Among these cities, rank products by their overall sales (still excluding promotions) in those quarters and take the top 20%. Then compute each top product’s share of total sales in Q4 2019 and Q4 2020 and calculate the difference in share from Q4 2019 to Q4 2020, returning the results in descending order of that share change.
sql:
WITH us_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    s.amount_sold,
    s.prod_id,
    c.cust_city,
    t.calendar_year
  FROM sales s
  JOIN customers c ON s.cust_id = c.cust_id
  JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id
  WHERE c.country_id = 52790
    AND s.promo_id = 999
    AND t.calendar_year IN (2019, 2020)
    AND t.calendar_quarter_number = 4
),
city_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    cust_city,
    SUM(CASE WHEN calendar_year = 2019 THEN amount_sold ELSE 0 END) AS sales_q4_2019,
    SUM(CASE WHEN calendar_year = 2020 THEN amount_sold ELSE 0 END) AS sales_q4_2020
  FROM us_sales
  GROUP BY cust_city
  HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN calendar_year = 2020 THEN amount_sold ELSE 0 END) >= 
         1.20 * SUM(CASE WHEN calendar_year = 2019 THEN amount_sold ELSE 0 END)
     AND SUM(CASE WHEN calendar_year = 2019 THEN amount_sold ELSE 0 END) > 0
),
qualifying_cities AS (
  SELECT cust_city FROM city_sales
),
prod_city_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    us.prod_id,
    us.calendar_year,
    SUM(us.amount_sold) AS prod_sales
  FROM us_sales us
  WHERE us.cust_city IN (SELECT cust_city FROM qualifying_cities)
  GROUP BY us.prod_id, us.calendar_year
),
overall_product_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    prod_id,
    SUM(prod_sales) AS total_sales
  FROM prod_city_sales
  GROUP BY prod_id
),
top_products AS (
  SELECT prod_id
  FROM (
    SELECT 
      prod_id,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY total_sales DESC) AS rn,
      COUNT(*) OVER () AS cnt
    FROM overall_product_sales
  )
  WHERE rn <= CAST(CEIL(cnt * 0.2) AS INTEGER)
)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM top_products
